correctness.rationale: PASS: The monomial projection formula follows from normalized area integrals; direct two-step composition gives a single nonzero anti-diagonal at each monomial degree sum, with only a possible central zero. Polynomial-pencil row reduction isolates a unique top-degree pair, yielding a triangular minor of size r+s−1 (odd sum) or r+s−2 (even sum). The bilinear harmonic pairing makes the finite matrix skew-symmetric after positive diagonal scaling, so the even-sum upper bound matches the minor. The centered Wronskian degree equals r+s−1. The commutator annihilates analytic vectors and maps anti-analytic vectors into analytic polynomials, proving square zero. The direct-composition checker passed 1305 exact-rational cases, independently forming the Wronskian; these are supplemental only.

originality.rationale: PASS with a bibliographic reservation: Cui–Huang–Lu–Zu (2026), Theorem 2.8, classifies when such commutators are finite rank, and their Corollary 3.1 gives square zero, but the complete polynomial-pair exact rank is not stated. Dong–Zhou treats quasihomogeneous symbols and determines individual monomial ranks, whereas a general two-polynomial pencil includes interacting monomial degrees and potential top-degree cancellation. Chen–Koo–Lee (2013) proves evenness and realization of even ranks according to the accessible abstract, but the full article was unavailable for checking. No searched indexed claim explicitly supplied or logically dominated the new exact formula; absence from an index alone does not establish priority.
residual_risks: The complete 2013 Chen–Koo–Lee article was inaccessible, so a polynomial-pair rank theorem there cannot be excluded.
An unindexed earlier equivalent rank law or a consequence of an unexamined general theorem is possible.
The monomial special case and the general finite-rank/square-zero classification belong to prior literature, not to the new originality claim.

value.rationale: PASS: Finite-rank classification and even-rank realizability leave the actual rank of an arbitrary polynomial pair undetermined. A natural invariant—the centered Wronskian degree—gives a complete exact rank formula, invariant under changes of basis of the polynomial pencil. The law identifies when lower-degree perturbations preserve rank and when cancellation of equal-degree leading terms shifts it, providing a structural classification rather than a single computed example.
